Software

watchengine + batwatch

Project details

watchengine ↗   batwatch ↗

Why I built them
I wanted a way to check whether a watch or car listing was actually priced well. I built two Python tools to collect listings, compare prices, and narrow down which ones were worth a closer look.
How they work
watchengine compares watch listings with prices for the same reference. batwatch looks at Bring a Trailer auctions and estimates the room left after purchase fees, tax, transport, and other costs. Both keep data in SQLite so I can compare listings across runs.
The hard part
The comparison only helps if the underlying items are similar. The tools track comparable sales and use minimum sample requirements. A flag is a reason to investigate a listing, and I am still checking the live results.

Advocacy · Community · Racing

Mountain Biking

Trail advocacy with CAMTB, a 30+ member riding club, and racing with brand sponsorships.

Project details
California Mountain Biking Coalition
As a CAMTB Teen Ambassador in 2025–2026, I traveled to Sacramento to advocate for trail access, youth outdoor programs, and public lands funding in support of the California Outdoor Recreation Partnership. I met with legislative staff from the offices of Assembly Members Juan Alanis, Al Muratsuchi, and Alexandra M. Macedo. Our small Teen Ambassador cohort also supported CAMTB’s broader advocacy around SCR 94, which designated June 2025 as California Mountain Biking and Trail Stewardship Month.
East Bay Mountain Biking Club
The previous school bike club had become inactive, so I started the East Bay Mountain Biking Club. I grew it to more than thirty members and established a partnership with First Mile Cycle Works, a local bike shop.
Racing & sponsorships
I raced with Miramonte High School’s branch of the Contra Costa Composite Mountain Biking Team. Through direct outreach to brand partnership teams, I secured sponsorships from Wheeled Lyfe Apparel and Hammer Nutrition during 2023–2026.
